newsitem.title: JAPAN: Crudes weaken in Asia, Minas stable on demand. [CORRECTED 09:40 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Crudes weaken in Asia, Minas stable on demand. [CORRECTED 09:40 GMT]

text.p: Crude oil prices weakened in Asia on Monday, depressed by expectations Iraq would begin limited crude oil exports soon, while regional crudes such as Minas and Tapis were steady in the wet market, traders said.
The end to a strike at three French refineries also depressed the market, a broker said.
(Corrects to show strike at refineries over)
Iraq oil minister, Amir Muhammed Rasheed, was reported as saying on Friday that Iraq expects to be able to resume oil exports from 0500 GMT on Tuesday.
January cash Brent was notionally assessed at $24.20/24.30.

The level was down from late Friday U.S. trading levels of $24.45/24.55. In spreads, February Brent/Dubai was bid at $1.87 and offered at $1.95, compared with late U.S. trading levels of $1.88/1.93. March Brent/Dubai was notionally assessed at $1.80/1.90.
A January/February Dubai swap was done between a Wall Street trader and a major at 60 cents, and a February/March Dubai swap was traded between the same trader and a different major at 69 cents.
In the wet market, a producer continued to offer January Tapis at a premium of $1.10 above quotes.

Bids were indicated at a premium of around 90 cents with possible buyers seen in Singapore and Thailand. The firm Tapis prices were products driven and largely attributable to seasonal requirements for kerosene and gas oil, traders said. Paper Tapis was assessed at $24.70.
Elsewhere in Asian crudes, January Minas was also assessed steady to firm with premiums assessed at about 50 cents above the official selling price.
Among Gulf crudes, February Oman was heard bid at around MPM plus eight to 10 cents. Some traders said the medium crude could weaken a bit once Iraq begins limited crude exports.
